coverage: Read-only aggregate review and legitimate pre-015 file compatibility; stable plans reject stale source, malformed files, symlinks and orphan SQL data.
Later-batch record trigger error and late authority-write trigger error roll back atomically. Owner authority is checked after locks and again immediately before commit.
A separate PDO connection kills the owned worker connection before its literal commit; failure preserves the original source and durable SQL-required intent, with no automatic file fallback.

All original collection keys and order, unknown fields, metadata timestamps, tokens, consent, suppression, frozen audiences and messages, queued recipients and every delivery outcome survive exact import and independent readback.

A selected-file write in a second runtime root holds the database data lock before activation; move remains blocked before first authorization, then subsequent operations use the shared SQL authority.
Two independent roots and four writers preserve all 52 mutations. An actual SQL update error rolls back without overwriting a concurrent state.
A database-wide delivery mutex prevents a losing worker from recovering or mutating the winning worker state; stopped-worker lock recovery distinguishes claimed from sending outcomes.
No SQL data transaction is held across SMTP. Actual loopback SMTP permits concurrent unsubscribe and pause, transmits no canceled message body and preserves unknown acceptance for review.

Stale snapshot saves cannot undo revocation. Missing state, authority or schema, record corruption, conflicting identities, guard mismatch, changed configuration and database outage fail closed after activation.
The full 190-character installation identity and normal metadata-only installation setting are accepted; explicit malformed, blank or conflicting secondary identities remain refused.

Historical installer classes were unchanged and the fixture was not modified to invent an identity.
